title: Selection-explanation emitter with near-miss disclosure
question: Implement the explanation record: for each selection, why this capability, which rule or score produced it, and which capabilities were near-misses that did NOT make the cut. Exact question: can an owner reading only the explanation reconstruct the decision without re-running the router?
claim_under_test: An owner given only the explanation record and the capability index can reproduce the selected set without re-running the router; near-misses that did not make the cut are named with a cutoff reason.
decision_procedure: 1. BAN beats every fusion score: a banned capability is never selected, whatever its score, and is disclosed as a near-miss with cutoff_reason=banned-by-owner-override.
2. PIN beats threshold and budget: a pinned capability (unless banned) is selected first, even below min_score, and its token_cost is charged to the budget before any scored candidate.
3. Remaining candidates are ranked by fusion_score descending; a candidate is selected when fusion_score >= min_score and its token_cost fits the remaining budget_tokens.

4. A candidate that was not selected is a near-miss when it was banned, when it scored >= min_score but did not fit the budget, or when it scored within near_miss_margin below min_score; every near-miss carries a cutoff_reason.
5. reconstruct.py reads the explanation only: the selected ids, in order, are the decision.
